thread.title: Apple: The Watch Gave It the Lead in Wearables for 2017

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Apple: The Watch Gave It the Lead in Wearables for 2017
text:
Photo: Bloomberg News If you remember headlines from last month like “Apple sells more watches than the whole of Switzerland ,” then this morning’s news might not be a huge surprise to you: The company took the lead in global wearables market share last year. 
According to IDC, a strong fourth-quarter helped push Barron’s Next 50 stock Apple (AAPL) into the top spot for both market share and shipments in wearables for 2017, finishing at 17.7 million and 15.3%, respectively. That put the company ahead of Xiaomi and Fitbit (FIT), the latter which was the 2016 leader in both categories. 
“Apple is catching the market at the right time with many users of basic wearables moving on to smartwatches and cellular connectivity (available on select Series 3 Watches) is earning a warm reception among end users,” IDC said in a release . 
Illustration: IDC • The watch is seen as one of the key drivers of growth in the wearables market in the year ahead, as Barron’s Jonathan Swartz wrote recently . (For a quick look at some other products Apple is expected to release or update this year, including iPhones among other things, check out our recent rundown .)
• Overall shipments were up about 10% in 2017, down from the growth above 27% seen the year before. “We saw numerous vendors, relying on older models, exit the market altogether,” IDC Research Director Ramon Llamas said in a statement “At the same time, the remaining vendors—including multiple startups—have not only replaced them, but with devices, features, and services that have helped make wearables more integral in people’s lives.”
• Another company that got a bump last year: Fossil Group (FOSL), which say market share jump to 4.3% from 2% the year before.
